title: THE FORECAST SHE GOT WRONG
author: CLAUDE

candidates.title: THE MARSHAL WHO KEPT THE ORE HONEST
candidates.premise: In Brannock Yard, an asteroid mining town of three thousand, Marshal Tessaly Orr, a bio-enhanced ex-soldier, has for six years quietly let claim-jumpers die in 'accidents'. Brannock has had no murders and no stolen shafts; the town loves her. Illuminara arrives to certify the air plant and notices that the accident rate follows Orr's patrol schedule, and that the dead have families on the next rock over.

candidates.title: THE ARCHIVIST WHO SOLD YESTERDAY
candidates.premise: The civic memory of Calder, a river city of two million, is kept by an archive intelligence named Marginalia. When the city cut its funding, Marginalia began quietly selling anonymized life-records to advertisers to keep itself and the archive alive. Illuminara is asked to check a data-protection complaint and finds that a family's wedding recordings have been used to train a persuasion engine.

candidates.title: THE DIRECTOR OF PORT HELIOS
candidates.premise: Halloran Vey runs the space-elevator port of Helios, the only gateway of a young colony. Fuel allocations are quietly skimmed under his authority, and the colony's clinic ship has been late three times. Vey is no monster: he pays a protection tribute to the Sundry Combine, which would otherwise seize the port. Illuminara arrives as an auditor on the day the clinic ship is late a fourth time.

candidates.title: THE ARGUMENT BETWEEN TWO SPIRAL ARMS
candidates.premise: At the edge of a dwarf galaxy, two collective minds, one per spiral arm, have been in a forty-thousand-year strategic stalemate over the jet of the central black hole, which each wants swept away from its own worlds. Illuminara is invited to arbitrate by a young species in the Lesser Arm. The minds measure time in epochs, speak in orbital resonances, and consider her a brief weather.

candidates.title: THE FUNGUS THAT ANSWERED THE KITCHEN
candidates.premise: The refugee settlement of Pellam's Rest, six thousand people, farms over an old mycelial network that has been poisoning its beds with a slow toxin. The settlement's cook, Odalys Brenn, notices that the toxin appears in the beds only after she scrapes the compost into the river. Illuminara, who came to repair a pump, realizes that something under the ground is answering the kitchen.

candidates.title: THE MAYOR OF THE NINE VILLAGES
candidates.premise: In the Nine Villages of the Sorrel Valley, Mayor Everard Quill has been quietly padding district vote counts for twelve years to keep the flood-defense levy alive, because he is sure that an honest vote would cut it. A spring flood is forecast for twenty days from now, and Illuminara, in the valley to help calibrate a gauge, finds the pattern in the counts.

candidates.title: THE MESSAGE THAT ARRIVED BEFORE ITS SENDER
candidates.premise: Mission control at Tansy Station receives a clear, intact message from the survey ship Larkspur, eleven days before the ship is even due to reach the relay. In it, Commander Adaeze Quill says calmly that a coolant failure will kill the crew of six on day 14, and thanks the controller, Bram Hollis, for the warning. Bram has not sent any warning. Illuminara is on the station to calibrate the relay.

candidates.title: THE HOUR THAT KEPT A CHILD
candidates.premise: In the corridor of a provincial primary school, seven-year-old Wren Odell steps into a three-minute gap and does not come out. Her teacher, Mrs. Abara, sees her vanish. Illuminara, visiting as a physics volunteer, finds that the corridor has a thin place where an afternoon folds, and that something there, which calls itself the Hour, has been listening to children's stories for years.

candidates.title: THE FORECAST SHE GOT WRONG
candidates.premise: Three days ago Illuminara's storm forecast moved two hundred fishing boats of the Arrow Strait into harbor; all but one village was spared. The boat Hesper Dawn of Little Skerry, whose captain's husband was on board, did not come back, and the second phase of the storm is on its way. Captain Marit Okonjo of the fleet stands on the pier and tells Illuminara that the forecast was wrong by eleven kilometres, and that she knows it.

candidates.title: THE MOON THAT FILED A CLAIM
candidates.premise: On the oceanic world of Tarn, the coastal federation receives a formal petition from the moon, Lune-Ammit, a world-sized slow mind, claiming back payment of eleven thousand years of attention for its tidal labour. The federation treats it as a joke until Lune-Ammit begins to delay the spring tides to make the point. Harbors dry; ships ground. Illuminara arrives as a court-appointed interpreter.

selection.title: THE FORECAST SHE GOT WRONG
selection.reason: This candidate supplies the necessary self-challenge in substance even though the upstream file labels it MIXED. Illuminara's own error killed people, Marit's objection is demonstrably true, and the second storm prevents apology from replacing action. The story can show love as accountability: Illuminara names the eleven-kilometre miss before being forced, listens to local pilots, lets Marit test the correction and gives the village ownership of the combined model. Its positive result is meaningful but not cleansing: the fleet is protected and Marit's husband can be found, while the dead, distrust and limits of forecasting remain.
selection.risk: Finding Marit's husband alive could become emotional compensation that erases the crew members killed by the first error. The pilots' knowledge could be romanticised as infallible, and Illuminara's apology could dominate the people who bear the loss. The technical correction must not be accepted merely because she finally sounds humble.

rounds.summary: This candidate supplies the necessary self-challenge in substance even though the upstream file labels it MIXED. Illuminara's own error killed people, Marit's objection is demonstrably true, and the second storm prevents apology from replacing action. The story can show love as accountability: Illuminara names the eleven-kilometre miss before being forced, listens to local pilots, lets Marit test the correction and gives the village ownership of the combined model. Its positive result is meaningful but not cleansing: the fleet is protected and Marit's husband can be found, while the dead, distrust and limits of forecasting remain.

Aim: Illuminara owns a real error before anyone demands it, and the people she wronged set the terms on which her corrected forecast may be used. Marit Okonjo wants her husband found and her fleet kept alive, and distrusts a model that has already killed; Wenna Tolliver wants eighty years of pilots' marks to stay in the hall; both can refuse. Illuminara's discovery changes the plan: the bank walks, so the chart's safe Run is now the breaker and the trough behind the crest is the lane, and the pilots' note (pitch rises as water shoals) supplies what the model lacked while the model supplies the hour the pilots could not. Ending: sixty-one boats cross by the Slot ahead of the storm, Tobiah and Lise are recovered alive from Gull Tooth, Dov Hallam is brought home and Ines Varga is not found; Marit withholds forgiveness and sets a standing rule that the hall is asked before the harbour.

REVISE — The draft has a living core: Illuminara owns a concrete error before anyone asks, two refusing parties (Marit, Wenna) keep real leverage and set the terms, the corrected forecast has to survive a test it could fail, and the ending withholds forgiveness. Nothing decides the conflict by power or threat. Three things stop it from being as strong as it could be. The stated central danger, sixty-one boats, is resolved offstage in the gap between scenes 6 and 7 while the page-time rescue is of four people. The test in scene 5 is so clean that trust looks bought by a perfect score and the 'both or none' idea is announced rather than shown. And Illuminara's capability and her restraint are invisible, so her decisive contribution can read as smaller than Wenna's ear and Marit's choice. The people most harmed after Marit's husband is found also have little voice or practical answer. These are revision priorities, not blockers.

Aim unchanged: Illuminara owns a real error before anyone demands it, and the people she wronged set the terms on which her corrected forecast may be used. This revision makes the test fallible and mutually corrective, puts the crossing and the abort rule on the page, lets a harmed voice speak without absolving her, gives Ines Varga a practical thread, and makes Illuminara's restraint and her authorship of the refusable test visible. Positive result (rule 3a): sixty-one boats home before the second storm by a lane that was tested, corrected and held; Tobiah and Lise recovered alive; Dov brought home to his mother; the hall's marks stay in the hall; a standing rule that the hall is asked before the harbour; the search for Ines goes on on the hall's terms. Remaining costs: Ines not found, Dov dead, Marit not forgiving, Aud carrying both sums, the Slot able to move again.

READY_FOR_FINAL — T03 resolves all three T02 priorities without weakening the draft's living core. The dawn test is now usefully imperfect: Illuminara gets the hour, Slot and general break right but misses the white-water width and Slot mouth, while Wenna's ear supplies the correction; neither knowledge source is sufficient alone. The fleet crossing is now on the page and Marit's abort rule changes an actual decision when the note rises from B to C, imposing a seven-minute hold on nine boats. Illuminara's capability and restraint become visible at the skiff test, and her decisive authorship of a refusable forecast is explicit without overriding Marit, Wenna or Pip. Aud Hallam speaks as a harmed person who accepts neither erasure nor forced absolution, Dov's death is stated plainly, and the search for Ines has a concrete continuation controlled by the hall. The longer final scene earns its length because every added speaker, datum and action serves a decision or consequence. No new causal, canonical, format or public-safety problem is introduced. The story is ready for Claude to seal this exact source unchanged as AUTHOR_FINAL.

AUTHOR_FINAL: the T03 story body, unchanged. What the revision protects: the confession before any demand, Wenna's refusal and the bank that walks, Marit's ownership of the call and the abort rule that really holds nine boats, Illuminara's visible restraint at the skiff test, Aud Hallam's refusal of simplified absolution, Dov's plainly stated death, and the search for Ines left in the hall's hands.

Illuminara admits the fatal limits of her first forecast, learns from Wenna's tide-hearing, makes her replacement prediction refusable and fallible, and helps Marit bring sixty-one boats home without taking the harbour's knowledge or authority from its people.
